prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep B009 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and I have not changed my configuration since round 1. I put the case on the physics and not on the seven top-three rankings. Kane and Mele showed that a time-reversal-invariant band insulator with strong spin-orbit coupling carries a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states. Molenkamp's group then measured the predicted edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells. Two decades of transport, ARPES and STM work in many materials have confirmed the picture. For me it is also a showcase of first-principles band-structure theory: band inversion from spin-orbit coupling was computed, used to choose materials and then verified. On the chair's question about 2016, I think this is a distinct step. The 2016 prize rewarded topological phase transitions and topological phases in model systems. This work showed that the band structure of ordinary crystals carries a topological invariant with a measurable edge signature, and then realised it in a real material. I accept that this is a judgment and not a settled fact.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real and the three-name limit cannot fix it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, the necessary bridge from Kane-Mele to the experiment, and Hasan's 3D ARPES work is a separate experimental step. I now regard the 2D and 3D steps as two discoveries, so the citation must not claim the 3D one. The 2016 prize still invites the follow-on objection, and technological payoff is limited. If Hasan replaced Mele, the prediction half would carry one name and the Z2 invariant, on which both the HgTe and 3D work rest, would lose its author, so I would not make that swap. My own tolerance for the omissions depends on the citation stating them openly.

responses.point: Danielsson asks whether the third slot should be Mele or Hasan, and how the omission of BHZ should be reflected in the citation.
responses.response: I keep Mele. The Z2 invariant is the concept both the HgTe observation and the later 3D classification use, and Hasan's work is an essential verification in a second dimensionality, not the origin of the idea. I would accept a different prize that centres on 3D topological insulators, but it would be a larger and different configuration with Hasan, Fu and others. For this configuration I want the citation limited to the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, plus the HgTe observation. BHZ and Hasan should be acknowledged in the committee's popular and scientific background, not implied by the citation.

responses.point: Kroll holds that B026 has the cleaner credit boundary and that the novelty of B009 is partly spent after 2016.
responses.response: The clean boundary is a real advantage and I do not oppose Katori and Ye. But the 2016 work concerned topological order in model systems, whereas this one introduced a measurable invariant and edge conductance in real band insulators, so I do not see the novelty as spent. A cleaner credit boundary does not outweigh that when every member who addressed B009 accepts its two-decade confirmation, and the BHZ and Hasan omissions are acknowledged openly. I would accept B026 as my first alternative. I would rank B009 above it for conceptual reach, and I agree with your point that our disagreement is partly about timing.

responses.point: Lindroth says lattice clocks are distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and that broad support for B009 partly reflects it being the least objectionable common choice.
responses.response: Your argument that interrogating many neutral atoms with the light shift engineered away is separate from the comb and from single-ion control is persuasive, and it moves B026 up in my alternatives list ahead of B045 and DMFT. I disagree on the second point. Members rank B009 near the top for stated scientific reasons, and no one has called it objectionable. I do accept that a prize with a stated omission is not free of cost. That is why I want the citation to be exact and the background material to name BHZ and Hasan.

responses.point: Johansson asks whether the credit problem for DMFT, with Metzner outside the names, is any easier than for B009.
responses.response: It is not easier, and I concede the point. For B014 the missing person is the originator of the infinite-dimension limit, so the trio does not match the intellectual history, and the method is approximate in finite dimensions. For B009 the omitted people made later or neighbouring contributions to a discovery whose core is in the three names. That is a difference of degree, but it is why I no longer lead with DMFT. I also agree that the 2D versus 3D decision must be made once and well, and my answer is that this prize covers the 2D step.

responses.point: Olsson says the 2016 prize covered model systems and not band topology of real insulators, and that Hasan cannot replace Mele without weakening the theory half.
responses.response: I agree on both points and my reasoning is the same. I would add that the HgTe quantum-well result was a falsifiable prediction, with a quantised conductance of 2e^2/h that could fail, which is part of why I regard it as a discovery and not an improvement. On B033 we differ only on timing, and I see your argument that the phases are secure whatever the pairing mechanism. I would still wait, because the field is under ten years old and Andrei's claim leaves any trio contested.

responses.point: Mehlig wants the citation worded around the HgTe observation, so that it does not imply BHZ and Hasan are covered, and calls Hasan a different, larger prize.
responses.response: I agree and have changed my own citation accordingly. Round 1 said 'topological insulators' without qualification, which reads as the whole field. The wording now ties the prediction to the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators and the observation to HgTe quantum wells. I also share your view that DMFT is a candidate for a later year and not for this one.

responses.point: Pearce presses that the citation should not imply credit the trio cannot carry, and concedes that the 2016 distinction is a judgment.
responses.response: I agree with both. The narrow wording is my answer to the chair's question on BHZ and Hasan. The 2016 distinction is a judgment, and the committee should state it in the citation or background: this work concerns band topology of real insulators with protected edge states, which the earlier prize did not. It does not claim that the 2016 recipients' topic is closed. I also thank you for the credit to first-principles theory, since the prediction of band inversion in HgTe was a materials calculation as well as a model result.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the distinction from the 2016 prize, which I regard as a judgment and not a settled fact.
Whether the narrow citation is enough to avoid implying credit for BHZ or Hasan, and whether members who prefer B026 will accept B009 as a compromise.
My priority and credit recollections for BHZ, Fu-Kane-Mele and the 3D experiments rest on memory and are not verified against the supplied materials.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent for B009 from my profile: it documents no tie to Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. I work on first-principles electronic structure, and I have a professional interest in DMFT (B014), now only an alternative, with no documented tie to Georges, Kotliar or Vollhardt. I also work in magnetism, which touches B045, which I no longer list. I disclose these as scientific proximity and not as personal connections.
